manifest.hypothesis: POST /api/organizer/competition/:id/score (46 req/run, avg 3677 ms, max 16.9 s) deletes the competition's rows and then inserts one row per CSV line with autocommit (one fsync each), all while holding the tenant flock; duplicates per player are kept, so a tenant-1 competition holds ~80k rows and every ranking read (527/run, avg 2049 ms) walks them all under the same lock. Writing DELETE + multi-row INSERTs in one transaction and keeping only the last CSV row per player removes the per-row fsyncs, shortens the lock hold, and leaves one row per player for ranking/player/billing to read.

observations.summary: observe-after-002 (one run on the indexed stable): score upload 46x avg 3677ms max 16857ms; ranking 527x avg 2049ms; player 462x avg 1327ms with only indexed PK lookups (queueing); bench ScenarioScoreMap: organizer scenarios 1205/2378 are paced by uploads; competitionScoreHandler inserts row by row with NamedExecContext on the *sqlx.DB (autocommit).

allowedChanges.reason: competitionScoreHandler: dedupe rows per player (last wins), one transaction, chunked multi-row INSERT; response rows = CSV line count as before

manifest.changeSummary: competitionScoreHandler keeps the last row per player_id while reading the CSV, then runs DELETE and chunked multi-row INSERTs (500 rows) in one SQLite transaction; the lock is still taken for the whole handler; the rows field still reports the CSV line count.
manifest.expectedEffect: Upload latency drops from seconds to well under a second (one fsync instead of N); ranking reads one row per player instead of every uploaded row, so ranking/player latency on the big tenant drops too; organizer scenarios iterate faster and fewer player workers leave; score up beyond the +9% band (plan item 2). Risk: ranking tie order must stay by row_num of the retained row (same row the old code picked).

ruleDecision.reason: median improved 1020 bp but worst candidate 2504 does not clear best baseline 2708; noise not separated

override.reason: rule: inconclusive (median +1020 bp: 2504/2641/2678 vs 2269/2389/2404/2708; the 2708 baseline sample is the outlier the worst candidate must clear). Override to promote: plan item 3 (drop the reader flock) is only correct once the upload writes DELETE+INSERT atomically, which this change does; all candidates beat the baseline median by >= 450 bp. Mechanism note from the candidate's app log: upload 3677 -> 3050 ms avg, ranking 2049 -> 1462 ms, player 1327 -> 1672 ms: the per-row fsync was not the cost; the upload's time is waiting for the tenant flock and dispensing ids on MySQL per row while holding it. Prediction 'well under a second' was wrong.
